userStories.title: Build the decisions list from memory rows
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the shared ReviewDecision wire type and the pure bounded memory-to-decisions builder.

**Motivation** — `nax bot review` remembers its own threads on one PR, but nothing carries over to the next PR: a finding a maintainer pushed back on comes back on the next PR that touches similar code.

**Approach** — Spec calls 3–5 (verbatim):

3. **Selection (design D3).** Two groups of the project's `MemoryItem` rows with `kind = DECISION`, `status = active`, `deletedAt = null`, and `ttlAt` null or later than the dispatch time (the same `OR [{ ttlAt: null }, { ttlAt: { gt: now } }]` the default `findByProjectMemory` read uses); both groups filter on the project id:
   - **recorded:** `sourceType` null or any value other than `review_event`; project-wide (a Prisma `sourceType: { not: 'review_event' }` alone drops NULL rows, so the filter is `OR [{ sourceType: null }, { sourceType: { not: 'review_event' } }]`);
   - **review-minted:** `sourceType = review_event` and `subject = repo:<repoId>` (only this job's repo).
   Recorded fill first, then review-minted, each ordered `updatedAt` desc then `id` desc, 100 in total (nax's cap). A review-minted row never pushes out a recorded one.
4. **Entry shape.** `id` = the memory item id; `source` = `koda:memory/<id>`; `statement` = `<predicate>: <object>`, or the predicate alone when `object` is null or empty. **"Characters" means UTF-16 code units (JS `string.length`), as nax's zod `.max(2000)` counts.** A statement longer than 2000 code units is cut to its first 1997 code units plus `...`; when the 1997th code unit is a high surrogate, the cut takes 1996 instead, so no lone surrogate is left.
5. **Byte cap.** When `Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify({ version: 1, decisions }))` is above 262,144 (nax's file cap), entries are dropped from the end of the ordered list until it fits. The runner writes exactly that compact serialization (call 7), so the file size equals the measured size.

Target integration (verbatim):
- `packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts` (types only) — Baseline: `review?: { prNumber: number; botLogin: string }`. Target: `review?: { prNumber: number; botLogin: string; decisions?: ReviewDecision[] }` with exported `interface ReviewDecision { id: string; statement: string; source?: string }`.
- New `apps/api/src/memory/review-decisions.ts`: `REVIEW_EVENT_SOURCE = 'review_event'`, `MAX_REVIEW_DECISIONS = 100`, `MAX_DECISION_STATEMENT = 2000`, `MAX_DECISIONS_FILE_BYTES = 262144`, `reviewRepoSubject(repoId): string` (`repo:<repoId>`), and the pure `buildReviewDecisions(recorded: MemoryItem[], reviewMinted: MemoryItem[]): ReviewDecision[]` applying calls 3-5 to rows already filtered and ordered by the repository.
- `ReviewDecision` is imported with `import type` from `@nathapp/fleet-protocol` (the API's protocol rule).

**Scope** — In: shared types, constants, subject formatting, ordered concatenation, statement formatting/truncation, count/byte caps and new co-located unit tests. Out: repository filtering and DI service (US-002), job persistence/dispatch (US-003), runner parsing/argv/files (US-004–006), and part-B decision minting. Feature boundaries: Turning `bot-review.json` events into `DECISION` items, the GitHub permission check, and the retire route; those are part B (feature `fleet-review-ingest`). Path-scoped decision selection; `MemoryItem` has no file paths, so every eligible decision is sent up to the cap. The pure builder does not query, sort or mutate memory rows.

**Interface** — Spec declarations:
```typescript
export interface ReviewDecision { id: string; statement: string; source?: string }
// AssignPayload field:
review?: { prNumber: number; botLogin: string; decisions?: ReviewDecision[] };
// review-decisions.ts exports:
REVIEW_EVENT_SOURCE = 'review_event'
MAX_REVIEW_DECISIONS = 100
MAX_DECISION_STATEMENT = 2000
MAX_DECISIONS_FILE_BYTES = 262144
reviewRepoSubject(repoId): string
buildReviewDecisions(recorded: MemoryItem[], reviewMinted: MemoryItem[]): ReviewDecision[]
```

Use optional/nullish MemoryItem.object semantics from the existing repository mapper. Test ASCII and surrogate-pair boundaries and measure the complete compact versioned wrapper, not just the array. Workdir is apps/api per binding structure; the protocol edit is explicitly included in this story.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] reviewRepoSubject('r1') returns 'repo:r1'.

[unit] buildReviewDecisions given one recorded row with id 'm1', predicate 'auth' and object 'tokens live in Redis' returns [{ id: 'm1', statement: 'auth: tokens live in Redis', source: 'koda:memory/m1' }].

[unit] buildReviewDecisions given a row whose '<predicate>: <object>' is 2500 ASCII characters returns an entry whose statement.length is 2000, ends with '...', and starts with the first 1997 characters of '<predicate>: <object>'.
[unit] buildReviewDecisions given a row whose '<predicate>: <object>' is exactly 2000 code units returns that text unchanged as the statement.
[unit] buildReviewDecisions given a row whose '<predicate>: <object>' is 2500 code units of emoji (each a surrogate pair) returns an entry whose statement.length is at most 2000.
[unit] buildReviewDecisions given a row whose '<predicate>: <object>' is 2500 code units of emoji (each a surrogate pair) returns an entry whose statement contains no lone surrogate.

routing.reasoning: Small additive protocol change plus a pure builder with explicit ordered/count/UTF-16/byte algorithms; no persistence or credential path changes.

userStories.title: Select a review's decisions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Select eligible recorded and repo-specific review-minted project decisions through an injectable memory service.

**Motivation** — koda already stores project decisions (`MemoryItem` kind `DECISION`).

**Approach** — Spec call 3 (verbatim):

3. **Selection (design D3).** Two groups of the project's `MemoryItem` rows with `kind = DECISION`, `status = active`, `deletedAt = null`, and `ttlAt` null or later than the dispatch time (the same `OR [{ ttlAt: null }, { ttlAt: { gt: now } }]` the default `findByProjectMemory` read uses); both groups filter on the project id:
   - **recorded:** `sourceType` null or any value other than `review_event`; project-wide (a Prisma `sourceType: { not: 'review_event' }` alone drops NULL rows, so the filter is `OR [{ sourceType: null }, { sourceType: { not: 'review_event' } }]`);
   - **review-minted:** `sourceType = review_event` and `subject = repo:<repoId>` (only this job's repo).
   Recorded fill first, then review-minted, each ordered `updatedAt` desc then `id` desc, 100 in total (nax's cap). A review-minted row never pushes out a recorded one.

Target integration (verbatim):
- `PrismaMemoryItemRepository` gains `findReviewDecisionRows(projectId, repoId, take): Promise<{ recorded: MemoryItem[]; reviewMinted: MemoryItem[] }>` (both groups, filtered and ordered per call 3, at most `take` each).
- New `apps/api/src/memory/review-decisions.service.ts`: `ReviewDecisionsService.selectForReview(projectId, repoId): Promise<ReviewDecision[]>`, provided and exported by `MemoryModule`.
- `ReviewDecision` is imported with `import type` from `@nathapp/fleet-protocol` (the API's protocol rule).

Seam (verbatim): `buildReviewDecisions` / `reviewRepoSubject` (US-001) are used by `ReviewDecisionsService.selectForReview` (US-002); the US-002 integration ACs run `selectForReview` against seeded rows and assert the returned list.

Standing rules (verbatim): memory is project-scoped (ADR-001: decisions from project P never reach a review in project Q), and the reviewer never writes memory itself.

**Scope** — In: bounded repository reads, service delegation to the upstream builder, MemoryModule provider/export wiring, PostgreSQL selection tests, and DI resolution in the existing module unit suite. Out: changing the pure builder/protocol contract (US-001), dispatch snapshots and FleetJobsModule import (US-003), runner delivery (US-004–006), part-B decision creation/retirement, and path-scoped selection. Feature boundaries: Turning `bot-review.json` events into `DECISION` items, the GitHub permission check, and the retire route; those are part B (feature `fleet-review-ingest`). Path-scoped decision selection; `MemoryItem` has no file paths, so every eligible decision is sent up to the cap.

**Interface** — Spec signatures:
```typescript
findReviewDecisionRows(projectId, repoId, take): Promise<{ recorded: MemoryItem[]; reviewMinted: MemoryItem[] }>
ReviewDecisionsService.selectForReview(projectId, repoId): Promise<ReviewDecision[]>
```

Capture a single now for both groups, compose the independent TTL and recorded-source OR predicates under AND, map Prisma rows through the existing domain mapper, and pass MAX_REVIEW_DECISIONS as take before invoking buildReviewDecisions. Do not change findByProjectMemory or existing memory-write permissions. Preserve MemoryModule's existing forwardRef import cycle treatment. Modify apps/api/src/memory/memory.module.spec.ts by adding the resolution test; every existing assertion is unchanged. Create apps/api/test/integration/memory/review-decisions.integration.spec.ts using canRunDbTests and real service calls against PostgreSQL fixtures; run it outside the sandbox with bun run test:scoped. The module-resolution case remains a no-DB unit test using GlobalStubsModule.

userStories.title: Snapshot the decisions on dispatch and send them
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist the selected REVIEW decisions once at dispatch and expose that snapshot through ASSIGN and job detail without expanding list responses.

**Motivation** — Today koda never passes one: the K1 runner argv is `<nax> bot review <pr> --profile <chain>` (`apps/runner/src/executor/nax-process.ts`).

**Approach** — Spec calls 1, 2, 6, 10 and 11 (verbatim):

1. **One snapshot point.** Both dispatch paths (the route `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs` and the K1-B `ReviewHeadDispatcher`) go through `FleetJobsService.dispatch`. For a `REVIEW` only, `dispatch` asks `ReviewDecisionsService.selectForReview(projectId, repoId)` for the list, before the insert transaction, and stores it in the new `FleetJob.reviewDecisions` column. Every other command stores null.
2. **The list is the wire format.** `reviewDecisions` holds exactly the array sent to the runner, in nax's shape `{ id, statement, source }`, so the input of a past review can be read back from the job.
6. **Wire.** `AssignPayload.review` gains optional `decisions`. `buildAssignPayload` adds it only when the job's `reviewDecisions` is a non-empty array; an empty list or null sends no `decisions` key.
10. **Old rows.** A job row written before this feature has `reviewDecisions` null and behaves as an empty list.
11. **Old runners.** A runner built before this feature still reports `botReview: true` (its probe never checked `--decisions`) and its `parseAssign` copies only `prNumber` and `botLogin`, so it would run the review without decisions. koda-wk's runner runs from the same checkout as the API build, so the two are deployed together; no separate capability flag is added.

Target integration (verbatim):
- `FleetJob` (`apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma`): adds `reviewDecisions Json?`; migration `20261117090000_fleet_review_decisions`.
- `NewFleetJob` / `FleetJobRecord` (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/domain/fleet-job.domain.ts`): optional `reviewDecisions?: ReviewDecision[] | null`. In `prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts`, `toJob` casts the JSON column to `ReviewDecision[] | null`; `createJob` omits the key when `reviewDecisions` is undefined, writes `Prisma.DbNull` for an explicit null, and writes an array as `as unknown as Prisma.InputJsonValue` (the pattern the file's `update` uses for `stories` and `postRun`). `dispatch` passes the key only for `REVIEW`.
- `ReviewDecision` is imported with `import type` from `@nathapp/fleet-protocol` (the API's protocol rule).
- `FleetJobsService` constructor — Baseline: ends with `private readonly audit: AuditRecorder`. Target: adds a last parameter `private readonly reviewDecisions: ReviewDecisionsService`. `FleetJobsModule` imports `MemoryModule`.
- `buildAssignPayload` (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/assign-payload.ts`): call 6.
- `FleetJobDto` (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/dto/fleet-job.dto.ts`): adds `reviewDecisions` (array of `{ id, statement, source }` or null), filled by `FleetJobDto.from`; `summary` sets it to null.

Generation and DI notes (verbatim):
The `FleetJob.reviewDecisions` column and migration, the domain fields, `FleetJobsService.dispatch` storing the snapshot for `REVIEW`, `FleetJobsModule` importing `MemoryModule`, `buildAssignPayload` sending `review.decisions`, `FleetJobDto.reviewDecisions`; regenerates `openapi.json` and the CLI client (`bun run generate` from the repo root). Run `bun run db:generate` in `apps/api` after the schema and migration edits (the Prisma client under `apps/api/src/generated/prisma/` is git-ignored and must be regenerated before `toJob` and `createJob` type-check). Only the root `openapi.json` is tracked and changes; the CLI client regenerates into the git-ignored `apps/cli/src/generated/`. The `FleetJobsModule` -> `MemoryModule` import is exercised by the existing `apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.module.spec.ts` compile test.

Seams (verbatim):
- `ReviewDecisionsService.selectForReview` (US-002) is used by `FleetJobsService.dispatch` (US-003); the US-003 route ACs dispatch through `POST /api/projects/:slug/fleet/jobs` and assert the stored `reviewDecisions`.
- `PlacementService` (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/placement.service.ts:204-210`): re-reads the job with `findById`, calls `buildAssignPayload`, and writes the ASSIGN `FleetCommand` with that payload.

Failure behavior: the project with no active decisions stores []; ASSIGN omits decisions. A selector exception propagates as dispatch HTTP 500 and no job is inserted. Preserve existing authorization, repo ownership/GitHub checks, ticket guards, budget checks, transactional audit/activity, CAS placement and after-commit events. Do not catch the memory query and fall back to an empty list.

**Scope** — In: nullable column/migration, JSON mapping and optional domain fields, dispatch/service/module integration, detail/list DTO behavior, wire assembly, generation, unit/route integration tests and required positional mock updates. Out: selector algorithms (US-001–002), runner parser/probe/file work (US-004–006), recomputing decisions on requeue, a separate decisions capability, web presentation, CLI commands and part-B ingest/retirement. Feature boundaries: Showing the decisions sent on the web job page; the API job detail exposes them. A CLI command for the decisions sent; the generated CLI client is regenerated but no command is added. Recomputing the decisions on requeue; a requeued `REVIEW` keeps the list stored at dispatch. A runner capability flag for decisions support; a runner built before this feature drops `review.decisions`, so the runner and the API are deployed together (call 11). Decisions for `RUN`, `PLAN`, thread or config jobs; only `REVIEW` jobs carry them. GitLab reviews; K1 reviews GitHub repos only. Turning `bot-review.json` events into `DECISION` items, the GitHub permission check, and the retire route; those are part B (feature `fleet-review-ingest`). Keep the stored field out of mutable/requeue reset patches.

**Interface** — Spec declarations:
```typescript
// Prisma FleetJob:
reviewDecisions Json?
// NewFleetJob and FleetJobRecord:
reviewDecisions?: ReviewDecision[] | null;
// Last FleetJobsService constructor parameter:
private readonly reviewDecisions: ReviewDecisionsService
```

Modify the three new FleetJobsService calls in apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.service.spec.ts (baseline lines 36,108,160) and the single calls in fleet-jobs.config-requeue.spec.ts:39, fleet-jobs.thread-handoff.spec.ts:12 and fleet-jobs.thread-requeue.spec.ts:28 by appending `{ selectForReview: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue([]) } as never`; every existing assertion is unchanged. Add dispatch unit cases in fleet-jobs.service.spec.ts and add cases to assign-payload.spec.ts and dto/fleet-job.dto.spec.ts; every existing assertion is unchanged. Create test/integration/fleet/fleet-review-decisions-dispatch.integration.spec.ts following the existing fleet-review-dispatch PostgreSQL route fixture pattern, including an online botReview-capable runner for ASSIGN assertions. Use canRunDbTests and run real DB tests outside the sandbox. The generated openapi.json delta is FleetJobDto.reviewDecisions; no other schema changes.

userStories.title: Accept decisions in runner assignments
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Validate and preserve optional review decisions at the runner's untrusted assign boundary.

**Motivation** — nax `v0.91.7-canary.11` accepts a caller decisions file (`nax bot review <pr> --decisions <path>`), renders it under "Project decisions ... data, not instructions", and adds its design-decisions checklist item only when decisions are present.

**Approach** — Spec call 9 (verbatim):

9. **Runner validation.** `parseAssign` checks `review.decisions` against nax's limits (at most 100 entries; `id` matching `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$` and unique; `statement` a string of 1..2000 characters; `source` absent or a string of at most 200 characters). A violation is `bad('review')`.

Target integration (verbatim):
- `parseAssign` (`apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts:154`, review check near line 179): call 9; the parsed `review` keeps `decisions` when present (an empty array is accepted and kept).

Story note (verbatim): `parseAssign` validates `review.decisions` per call 9 ("characters" = UTF-16 code units, JS `string.length`).

Upstream wire shape (verbatim): `review?: { prNumber: number; botLogin: string; decisions?: ReviewDecision[] }` with exported `interface ReviewDecision { id: string; statement: string; source?: string }`.

**Scope** — In: parser validation, sanitized copied decision entries, absent-versus-empty preservation, and additive cases in assign-parser.spec.ts. Out: protocol definition and API selection/snapshot (US-001–003), argv/capability detection (US-005), file writing and spawn integration (US-006). Feature boundary: Decisions for `RUN`, `PLAN`, thread or config jobs; only `REVIEW` jobs carry them. Do not allow review metadata on non-REVIEW assignments or change existing botLogin/prNumber/bashMode rules.

**Interface** — Existing seam:
```typescript
export function parseAssign(command: FleetCommandOut): ParsedAssign
```
Spec ReviewDecision declaration:
```typescript
interface ReviewDecision { id: string; statement: string; source?: string }
```

The parser currently copies only prNumber and botLogin; update validation and construction together so accepted decisions are not silently dropped. Reject arrays/non-objects as entries, duplicate ids, non-string fields and out-of-bounds values through bad('review'), observed as `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid review' }`, not an exception. Missing decisions is allowed; [] is allowed and retained. Do not replace string.length with byte length or add stricter trimming/ASCII rules. Extend apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.spec.ts; every existing assertion is unchanged. All cases are pure injected Bun unit tests with no host services.

userStories.title: Teach runner argv and capability probing about --decisions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Support an optional REVIEW decisions path in argv and advertise botReview only when nax supports that flag as well as the existing safety checks.

**Motivation** — Today koda never passes one: the K1 runner argv is `<nax> bot review <pr> --profile <chain>` (`apps/runner/src/executor/nax-process.ts`).

**Approach** — Spec call 8 (verbatim):

8. **Probe.** The runner reports `botReview: true` only when, in addition to the K1 checks, `bot review --help` stdout contains `--decisions`. A nax without it stops being placed for reviews instead of failing every review on an unknown flag.

Target integration (verbatim):
- `buildNaxArgv` (`apps/runner/src/executor/nax-process.ts`) — Baseline: `buildNaxArgv(naxCommand, assign)`. Target: `buildNaxArgv(naxCommand, assign, opts: { decisionsPath?: string } = {})`; a `REVIEW` with `opts.decisionsPath` appends `'--decisions', opts.decisionsPath`.
- The nax probe's private `botReview` (`apps/runner/src/capabilities/nax-probe.ts:258`): call 8.

Regression fixture note (verbatim):
- `apps/runner/src/capabilities/nax-probe.spec.ts` — the test `US-004: advertises K0 only when bot review exists and rejects ambient token env` (line 67) stubs `bot review --help` with stdout `help`, which no longer yields `botReview: true` once the probe requires `--decisions`; its stub stdout becomes `--decisions <path>  Caller decisions file`, and its `botReview` and env assertions are unchanged; the file also gains tests for this story's probe acceptance criteria.

Spec call 11 (verbatim):
11. **Old runners.** A runner built before this feature still reports `botReview: true` (its probe never checked `--decisions`) and its `parseAssign` copies only `prNumber` and `botLogin`, so it would run the review without decisions. koda-wk's runner runs from the same checkout as the API build, so the two are deployed together; no separate capability flag is added.

Failure-table behavior (verbatim): nax on the runner lacks `--decisions` | The probe omits `botReview`; reviews stay QUEUED with misfit `bot_review`.

**Scope** — In: optional argv options, REVIEW flag ordering after --profile, positive/negative help probing, FakeNaxCli-backed tests, the required existing fixture update, and verification of the existing API QUEUED/bot_review regression without API code changes. Out: API placement-rule rewrites (the existing bot_review gate already applies), parser implementation (US-004), writing or passing the real file in HostExecutor.spawn (US-006), separate capability flags or daemon-wide minimum-version changes. Feature boundary: A runner capability flag for decisions support; a runner built before this feature drops `review.decisions`, so the runner and the API are deployed together (call 11).

**Interface** — Spec signature:
```typescript
buildNaxArgv(naxCommand, assign, opts: { decisionsPath?: string } = {})
```
Existing implementation retains `naxCommand: readonly string[]`, `assign: AssignPayload` and return type `string[]`.

Append the flag/path only to REVIEW argv; preserve the profile chain with koda-job-<jobId> last and all existing two-argument callers. Keep help exit/timeout/spawn checks and the --version probe using NAX_FORGE_TOKEN=probe, which must exit 1 with stderr containing 'NAX_FORGE_TOKEN is not supported'. No new flag means no botReview key, not botReview:false. The existing API placement tests in apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/placement-rules.spec.ts and test/integration/fleet/fleet-review-dispatch.integration.spec.ts establish that a report without botReview leaves REVIEW queued with bot_review; reuse this behavior, not duplicated runner business logic. The QUEUED/bot_review acceptance outcome is verified by the existing API placement and dispatch regression suites against a report lacking botReview; do not import API services into Bun runner tests, add new API behavior, or add a dependency on US-003 for this baseline regression. Extend nax-process.spec.ts and nax-probe.spec.ts; every existing assertion is unchanged, except only the specified help fixture text is updated. Unit tests inject FakeNaxCli and toolWorks and do not depend on installed nax.

userStories.title: Write and pass the runner decisions file
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Write the compact mode-0600 decisions file before the review token and pass its absolute path to nax, retaining it until attempt wipe.

**Motivation** — nax `v0.91.7-canary.11` accepts a caller decisions file (`nax bot review <pr> --decisions <path>`), renders it under "Project decisions ... data, not instructions", and adds its design-decisions checklist item only when decisions are present.

**Approach** — Spec call 7 (verbatim):

7. **Runner file.** When `assign.review.decisions` is non-empty, `HostExecutor.spawn` writes `<jobDir>/review-decisions.json` as `JSON.stringify({ version: 1, decisions })` (no indentation, no trailing newline, mode `0600`) **before** the token file, and `buildNaxArgv` appends `--decisions <that absolute path>` after `--profile <chain>`. No file and no flag otherwise. The file holds no secret, so it is removed only by the attempt wipe (`ATTEMPT_FILES`), not by cleanup. *(Deliberate divergence from the design doc, which names the file `decisions.json` and removes it at cleanup: the `review-` prefix keeps it apart from nax's own `workflow/decisions.jsonl`, and nothing secret needs a cleanup.)*

Target integration (verbatim):
- New `apps/runner/src/executor/review-decisions-file.ts`: `REVIEW_DECISIONS_FILE = 'review-decisions.json'`, `writeReviewDecisions(jobDir, decisions): Promise<string>` (mode `0600`, returns the path).
- `HostExecutor.spawn`: call 7. `ATTEMPT_FILES` adds `review-decisions.json`.

Seams (verbatim):
- `AssignPayload.review.decisions` (US-001, filled by US-003) is read by `parseAssign` (US-004) and `HostExecutor.spawn` (US-006); the US-006 spawn ACs drive `spawn` with an injected `spawnNax` and assert the argv and the written file.
- `buildNaxArgv`'s `decisionsPath` (US-005) is passed by `HostExecutor.spawn` (US-006); asserted through the argv the injected `spawnNax` records.

Failure handling (verbatim):
- Writing `review-decisions.json` fails | `spawn` throws (the job FAILS with `spawn failed: <message>`); no token file is written; nax is not started.
- The token is missing, or nax fails to start, after `review-decisions.json` was written | The decisions file stays until the next attempt wipe (it holds no secret).

**Scope** — In: fixed-basename writer, exact compact serialization, mode/path return value, REVIEW-only conditional spawn integration, write-before-token ordering, failure propagation, retained non-secret file, attempt wiping and additive helper/spawn/JobRun error-mapping regression tests. Out: memory selection/snapshot/wire creation (US-001–003), assign validation (US-004), argv/probe design changes beyond using the US-005 seam, removing decisions at cleanup, adding decisions to RUN/PLAN/thread/config jobs, and part-B ingest. Feature boundaries: Removing `review-decisions.json` at job cleanup; it holds no secret and the attempt wipe removes it. Decisions for `RUN`, `PLAN`, thread or config jobs; only `REVIEW` jobs carry them. Preserve the separate secret forge-token lifecycle and never put the token value in argv, environment or decisions JSON.

**Interface** — Spec declarations:
```typescript
REVIEW_DECISIONS_FILE = 'review-decisions.json'
writeReviewDecisions(jobDir, decisions): Promise<string>
```
Use the upstream `ReviewDecision[]` for decisions and the existing absolute validated jobDir. The file bytes are exactly JSON.stringify({ version: 1, decisions }); use writeFile with mode 0o600 at creation like review-token.ts, not pretty JSON or an added newline. In HostExecutor.spawn, write only when job/assign command is REVIEW and decisions is non-empty, before reviewEnv can write forge-token. Then call buildNaxArgv with the returned decisionsPath. A failure writing the decisions file must propagate before token creation or spawnNax. Missing token continues to throw 'git token: none' after the non-secret file is written. A failed process start still removes any token as before but must not delete decisions. Existing JobRun maps spawn exceptions to FAILED with 'spawn failed: <message>'; reuse it instead of introducing transitions here. Exercise that existing error-to-state contract in apps/runner/src/supervisor/job-run.spec.ts with the injected spawnError pattern already used for missing-token and ENOENT failures; do not add supervisor business logic. Add REVIEW_DECISIONS_FILE to ATTEMPT_FILES so prepare wipes prior attempts, and do not add it to cleanup or token-removal code.

Create review-decisions-file.spec.ts with real temp files for parsed content, return path, stat mode and byte size. Extend apps/runner/test/unit/host-executor.spec.ts with injected spawnNax assertions of file/argv/failure ordering and prepare wiping; every existing assertion is unchanged. Force filesystem failure deterministically and check that the token file was never created. Keep assertions outside swallowed callbacks and do not require real sockets, host nax or processes for the new spawn cases.

Goal and completion: Fleet REVIEW jobs receive an immutable dispatch-time snapshot of eligible project decisions, persist the exact nax wire array, send it through ASSIGN, and run nax bot review with a compact caller decisions file. Completion includes both existing dispatch entry points, database persistence and job-detail visibility, protocol validation, capability gating, deterministic list/byte limits, and filesystem/error-ordering behavior. The six story IDs, workdirs and dependencies are binding; US-001 intentionally runs in apps/api despite also changing packages/fleet-protocol, as required by the spec. Relevant app sources of truth are .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md and .nax/mono/apps/runner/context.md. The root guidance specifies Nuxt 4 for web, which this feature does not change. API implementation agents must consult the nathapp-nestjs-patterns skill before writing NestJS code; no matching skill file was found in this checkout during planning. API imports of @nathapp/fleet-protocol must be type-only; never introduce a runtime protocol dependency in API production code.

This is an additive optional field, with no separate capability flag or protocol-version bump prescribed. Export ReviewDecision { id, statement, source? } and widen only the review block. apps/api/src/memory/memory-item-repository.ts:46 defines the domain MemoryItem; optional object and sourceType represent database nulls as undefined. apps/api/src/memory/prisma-memory-item.repository.ts:62 maps those nullable columns using ?? undefined, so the pure builder must accept nullish objects as well as empty string without coercing them into text. apps/api/src/common/enums.ts:93 defines MemoryKind.DECISION; use local constants, not Prisma enums. Selection/filtering and ordering are the repository's responsibility, not the pure builder's: preserve supplied order, concatenate recorded then review-minted, take at most 100, format statement/source, truncate UTF-16 safely, and drop the suffix until compact wrapper JSON fits 262144 bytes. Array length, string.length and UTF-8 bytes are distinct limits; do not truncate by Unicode code-point count or measure only the array. Optional hardening criteria are segregated as suggestedCriteria; required ACs retain the spec's story allocation, and failure-table outcomes are explicitly represented where not already covered. No memory writes, ingest/retire changes, new permission routes, or business-rule duplication in runner/UI are part of this feature.
